Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

  3
 MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For

development by ensuring that investments in parks, open spaces, green infrastructure and river
revitalization projects directly benefit residents and small businesses.

The Revitalization Plan identifies 155 multi-benefit project opportunity areas, including those that
could be located within or adjacent to South Gate. These projects address critical issues such as
improving water quality, expanding green space, enhancing public access, reducing heat island
effects, restoring habitat, and creating safe, connected pathways for pedestrians and cyclists. The
LLAR PT Report emphasizes that liousing stability and workforce pathways are essential to the
success of revitalization.  Without  these safeguards, public investments risk accelerating
gentrification  and displacement.  The campaign incorporates anti-displacement  measures,  local
hiring practices, and workforce training initiatives to ensure that residents share the economic  and
health benefits of the revitalized river corridor.

In addition, the RMC Consolidated Grant Program provides competitive funding for projects that
align with these goals, including land acquisition, park creation, habitat restoration, and climate
resilience improvements.  Suppoiting the Lower LA River Para Todos campaign positions the City
of South Gate to leverage future grant opportui'iities  for capital projects and community programs
which support environmental justice and sustainability.

  SUBJECT:  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  FOR  DEVELOPMENT  OF A
  STREET  SOCCER  USA  FACILTY  AT  HOLLYDALE  REGIONAL  PARK

  PURPOSE:  The purpose  of this item is to obtain  City  Council  approval  of a nonexclusive
  license  agreement  to Street Soccer USA  to use a portion  of the park for soccer prograrnmatic
  activities,  including  the installation  of a new artificial  turf  soccer field  to be temporarily  installed
  on city owned  property  for public  recreational  use, provided  the Contractor  maintains  ownership,
  maintenance,  and control  of the Soccer  Field  Site during  the term of this agreement.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:

  a.  Approve  the proposed  License  Agreement  with  Street Soccer USA;  and
  b.  Authorize  the City  Manager  to finalize  the terms  of the License  Agreement;  and
  c.  Waive  the building  permit  fees associated  with  the installation  of the facility.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  The proposed  lease agreement  would  result  in the development  of a
  privately  funded  soccer facility  valued  at approximately  $500,000,  to be constructed  and
  operated  for public  recreational  purposes  on approximately  10,000  square feet of Hollydale
  Regional  Park. The initial  lease term is five  (5) years, with  an option  to extend  upon mutual
  agreement  of both parties.

  The lease also provides  the City,  and/or  designated  community  organizations,  with  defined  hours
  of use of the facility  for public  prograrnrning  purposes.  There  is no anticipated  negative  fiscal
  impact  to the City.  Street Soccer USA  has agreed to aSSiSt with  weekday  park closures,  including
  securing  restroom  facilities  and park gates, thereby  eliminating  the need for additional  City
  staffing.  Street Soccer  USA  will  provide  staff to conduct  afternoon  and evening  restroom
  maintenance  and the restocking  of supplies  during  its permitted  use, reducing  operational
  demands  on City personnel.  Additionally,  Street Soccer  USA  will  provide  staff and/or  security
  persoru'iel  to monitor  participants  and visitor  safety  within  the park and adjacent  parking  areas
  during  prograrnrned  activities.  They  will  assist in maintaining  appropriate  noise levels  and

  10
 mitigating  potential  impacts  on surrounding  residential  neighborhoods.  As part of the project,
Street Soccer USA  has requested  a waiver  of building  permit  fees associated  with  the installation
of the facility,  in the atnount  of $5,146.27.  City  staff are supportive  of this request,  recognizing
that the project  is fully  privately  funded  and provides  substantial  community  benefits,  including
expanded  recreational  opportunities  for youth  and formalized  partnerships  with  local
organizations  such as AYSO.

REPORT  SUMMARY:  Street Soccer  USA  (SSUSA),  a national  nonprofit  organization,  in

partnership  with  VISA  and in connection  with  the 2026 FIFA  World  Cup, is implementing  a
nationwide  initiative  to construct  twenty-six  (26) community  soccer facilities  by 2026.  The
program  focuses  on expanding  access to safe, high-quality  soccer facilities  in underserved
communities  by providing  free and accessible  recreational  and youth  programming

SSUSA  has secured 'funding  for the design,  construction,  and installation  of these facilities  and is
currently  seeking  partner  locations.  In South  Gate, SSUSA  is already  working  with  local  schools
to provide  soccer programming  and has expressed  a desire to expand  and formalize  its presence
through  a permanent  facility  that would  support  school-based  programs,  community  groups,  and
youth  development  activities.

The proposed  partnership  would  also address  a documented  community  need for lighted  soccer
facilities,  particularly  during  the fall and winter  seasons. Local  AYSO  programs  currently  face
limited  access to fields  with  lighting  during  weekday  evening  hours.  SSUSA  has agreed to
coordinate  with  AYSO  to provide  access to field  space during  standard  practice  hours,  helping  to
alleviate  scheduling  constraints  and expand  recreational  opportunities  for local youth.

Under  the proposed  licensed  agreement,  SSUSA  would  design,  construct,  and install  the soccer
facility  from  start to finish  at no cost to the City.  The facility  would  include  FIFA-grade  artificial
turf,  four-foot  perimeter  walls,  sixteen-foot  netting,  a lighting  system,  and removable  walls  to
allow  for both small-sided  and full-field  play configurations.  The project  would  be located  within
a gated area of Hollydale  Regional  Park currently  utilized  by the Parks Maintenance  Division  for
equipment  and supply  storage.  SSUSA  would  occupy  the southern  portion  of the yard, while  the
northern  portion  would  remain  available  for continued  maintenance  operations.

On December  11, 2025, the Parks and Recreation  Commission  received  a presentation  on the
proposed  Street Soccer USA  project  and recommended  that the item be brought  forward  for City
Council  consideration.  On January  13, 2026,  City  Council  received  a presentation  on the
proposal  and directed  staff to return  with  a formal  agreement  between  the City  and Street Soccer
USA,  as well  as a separate  agreement  between  Street Soccer  USA  and AYSO,  to clearly  define
shared use, roles, and responsibilities.

The proposed  facility  would  consist  of two (2) 5-versus-5  soccer fields,  with  the option  to
convert  to one larger  field  as needed.  In addition,  the project  includes  a classroom  unit to support
after-school  engagement,  homework  assistance,  and educational  programming  tied to SSUSA's
youth  development  mission.
